**RaceFilter** is a Dalamud plugin for Final Fantasy XIV that hides and mutes players by race and/or gender through a configurable rule list. Each rule targets a race, a gender, or both, and independently controls three effects: hiding the model, blocking chat, and muting audio.

It ships with one default rule: hide, chat-block, and mute all Lalafells, with friends and Free Company members exempt.

## Features

* **Rule-based targeting:** any combination of race (Hyur, Elezen, Lalafell, Miqo'te, Roegadyn, Au Ra, Hrothgar, Viera, or "Any") and gender (Male, Female, or "Any"). Duplicate race+gender rules are prevented by the UI.
* **Three independent effects per rule:**
  * **Hide:** removes the model and nameplate
  * **Chat:** blocks their chat messages
  * **Mute:** silences their voice lines (emotes, battle shouts), footsteps, and ability/animation sound effects
* **Per-rule exemptions:** Friends and Free Company members (same home world) can be excluded per rule. Exempt players are fully untouched.
* **Content-safe by design:** grouped players and duties are protected automatically (see the behavior table below).
* **Far-away chat filtering:** a persistent race cache remembers every player you have seen, so chat from matched players is filtered even when they are out of render range. Never-seen senders always pass through.
* **Tooltips everywhere:** hover any checkbox in the config to see exactly what checked and unchecked mean.

## Behavior

| Who / where | Hide model | Block chat | Mute audio |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Matched player in the overworld | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ |
| Party / alliance member, anywhere | never | never | ✔ |
| Anyone, inside an instanced duty | never (paused) | never (paused) | ✔ |
| Exempt friend / FC member | never | never | never |

Party and alliance members always keep their model and chat visible, with no opt-out: you must be able to see, click-target, and read callouts from the people you are grouped with. Muting their audio is still allowed, and muting keeps working inside duties.

## Installation

1. Add my custom plugin repository: [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Valiice/DalamudPluginRepo/master/repo.json](https://github.com/Valiice/DalamudPluginRepo)
2. Search for **RaceFilter** in the Plugin Installer.
3. Install and Enable.

> **Note:** this plugin will never be on the mainline Dalamud repository; race-targeting plugins are not accepted there. It is only distributed through the custom repository above.

## Commands

* `/racefilter` - Opens the configuration window.
* `/racefilter toggle` - Flips the master on/off switch.

## Configuration

Open the config with `/racefilter`. Each row in the rules table is one rule:

| Column | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| **On** | Checked: the rule is active. Unchecked: ignored. |
| **Race / Gender** | Who the rule targets. "Any" matches everyone. Options that would duplicate another rule are hidden. |
| **Hide / Chat / Mute** | Checked: the effect is applied to matching players. |
| **Friends / FC** | Checked: those players are exempt and the rule never touches them. Unchecked: they are filtered like anyone else. |

The race cache counter at the bottom shows how many players the plugin has learned; **Clear cache** forgets them all (chat filtering for far-away players resets until they are seen again).

## Limitations

* A player's race can only be known once their character has rendered near you at least once (or is remembered in the cache). Chat from never-seen players always passes through.
* Cross-realm party members who are out of render range are exempt in party chat, but their tells/shouts may still be filtered (their party membership cannot be resolved remotely).
* The race cache persists on clean plugin unload; a game crash loses the current session's sightings.

## Troubleshooting

* **Someone is not being hidden?** Check they are not in your party/alliance or in a duty with you (both always show models), and that no Friends/FC exemption applies. Race is only known once they have rendered nearby.
* **Part of the audio muting stopped after a game patch?** The footstep and ability-sound hooks use byte signatures and memory offsets that can go stale on patches. Each hook degrades independently: the plugin keeps working (hide, chat, and the surviving mute paths) and logs the failure; update the plugin to restore the rest.
* **A friend's chat got filtered?** Make sure the rule's **Friends** exemption is checked, and that they are actually on your friend list (friendship is per-character in FFXIV).
